title: Privacy Policy
introDesc: This Privacy Policy describes how the hosted Oblivions website at msg.oblivions.ir handles information. The hosted service is operated by TwelveII (the “operator”, “we”, or “us”). Oblivions is currently provided through a web browser; we do not currently offer an official iOS, Android, or desktop app. This policy applies to the hosted website only. It does not automatically apply to independently operated servers or instances. If you connect to another operator’s instance, that operator is responsible for its own privacy practices. Please read this policy before using the service.
dataItem1: Account and profile information. We store your username, display name, password hash, and profile information you choose to provide, such as an avatar or wallpaper. An email address is optional and is used for account-related email, including password recovery.
dataItem2: Messages and encryption. Messages and direct messages are stored so they can be delivered and remain available in conversations. Where end-to-end encryption (E2EE) is enabled and correctly configured, message content is stored in encrypted form and the server operator cannot read that content. E2EE does not cover every piece of service metadata. If you report a message, the report includes a snapshot of up to 500 characters of its text: for encrypted messages this excerpt is supplied by the reporting client; for server-readable messages it can be copied by the server. Treat anything included in a report as disclosed to the moderation team.
dataItem3: Files and attachments. Images, videos, and other files you upload are stored so the service can deliver and display them. Files attached as evidence to a report are stored with that report. Deleting a message also deletes its attached message files through the website’s deletion flow.
dataItem4: Usage and service records. We handle account creation and activity timestamps, message and file metadata needed to operate the service, and records required to protect the service, prevent abuse, and troubleshoot faults.
dataItem5: Mobile push notifications are not part of the hosted web service currently offered. The website does not register your device with Apple Push Notification service (APNs) or Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM).
dataItem6: Signed-in browser session and connection information. Active-session records can include the browser or device label, IP address used by the session, approximate city and country, and sign-in/last-active timestamps. This information appears in Settings → Security so you can review and revoke sessions. Approximate location is resolved on the server using the DB-IP IP-to-city database; the lookup does not send your IP address to a separate geolocation provider. Session records are removed when sessions are revoked or expire under the service’s session rules.
dataItem7: Diagnostics and error reports. The web client may send technical error details such as an error message, a shortened stack trace, the website route, browser information, and client version. When you are signed in, a report may be associated with your account; reports from signed-out pages may not be. The client and server scrub common sensitive values such as authentication tokens, email addresses, identifiers, URL query parameters, and local home-folder names before storage. Scrubbing is not perfect: an error message may still contain a short fragment of data involved in the error. The service uses request IPs for rate limiting, but does not store the IP address as part of the client error record. Client error logs are retained for up to 30 days, subject to operational cleanup.
dataUsageDesc: We use information only as needed to provide, secure, support, and improve the hosted service, including to:
usageItem1: Create and maintain accounts; authenticate users; deliver messages, calls, and files; and provide account recovery when an optional email address is configured.
usageItem2: Operate active-session controls, investigate security incidents, prevent spam and abuse, review user and server reports, and enforce the Terms of Service.
usageItem3: Diagnose errors, maintain reliability, protect service infrastructure, respond to support requests, and meet applicable legal obligations.
noTrackingDesc: Oblivions does not use advertising networks, third-party analytics services, cross-site tracking pixels, or user profiling for targeted advertising. The service may use strictly necessary browser storage or similar technologies to keep you signed in and make core features work. Those functional technologies are not used to follow you across unrelated websites.
dataSharingDesc: We do not sell or rent personal information. Information is shared only when needed to operate a feature or address a legitimate service, safety, or legal need. This can include: the configured GIF search provider when you search for GIFs (the search request is forwarded without attaching your Oblivions account identity); the configured email-delivery provider for password recovery and administrative report notifications; and the configured LiveKit infrastructure for real-time voice/video. Those providers process the information needed for their specific function under their own terms and privacy policies. Reports and evidence are available to the service’s authorized moderation administrators. We may also disclose information when required by applicable law or necessary to protect users, the service, or others.
selfHostDesc: Voice and video traffic is handled by the LiveKit server configured for the instance. If you use the hosted msg.oblivions.ir service, that infrastructure is selected by its operator. If you configure a separate LiveKit server or connect to an independently operated Oblivions instance, the relevant operator may process connection and media information under its own policies. Using a self-hosted LiveKit server does not move your account, messages, or uploaded files away from the Oblivions instance you are connected to.
deletionDesc: We keep information for as long as needed to provide the service and for the purposes described in this policy. Session records are removed when revoked or expired; client error logs are kept for up to 30 days. Reports and report evidence may be retained for moderation, safety, and enforcement purposes; there is no promise that a report is erased when the reported message or account is deleted. You can request account deletion under Settings → Security. The account is deactivated immediately and can be restored during a 30-day grace period by signing in again with your password. After that period, profile information, uploaded files, push tokens, and other personal account data are removed as part of the deletion process. Messages may remain where needed for conversation continuity, but are attributed to “Deleted User”; the other participants may continue to see the conversation. Some records may be retained where necessary for security, moderation, legal compliance, or the establishment or defence of claims.
contactDesc: You can manage profile details, optional email, and signed-in browser sessions on the website. You can delete individual messages and request account deletion through Settings → Security. Depending on applicable law, you may have additional rights to access, correct, or request deletion of personal information. To ask a privacy question or make a request, use the contact option on the website. No public contact email is provided. We may need to verify that a request is yours before acting on it.
delIntro: You can request deletion of your hosted Oblivions account from the website. No email is required.
delStep1: Open the Oblivions website and sign in to the account you want to delete.
delStep2: Open Settings and go to the Security section.
delStep3: Find Delete account and choose the delete action.
delStep4: Review the warning and confirm your request.
delDataTitle: What happens after you request deletion
delData1: Your account is deactivated and you are signed out immediately. For 30 days, you can cancel the request by signing in again with your password. After the grace period, deletion proceeds.
delData2: Your profile information, uploaded files, push tokens, and other personal account data are removed as part of the deletion process. Security, moderation, or legal records may be retained where necessary.
delData3: Some messages may remain so conversations continue to make sense, but your identity is replaced with “Deleted User”. Other participants may still see messages in their conversations.
delPartialIntro: You can also manage some information without deleting your account:
delPartial1: Messages: delete a message you sent using its Delete action in the web interface. The deletion flow also removes files attached to that message.
delPartial2: Email address: your email is optional and can be removed in Settings → Security.
delPartial3: Profile: change or remove your avatar, wallpaper, and profile details in Settings.
